chapter: After Cab: Don Redman, teaching and records
title: Paying the band in odd change and the savings-account idea
summary: As paymaster at $66.66 a week, Thomas drew exact change and proposed a band savings account, which the men soon quit.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I had another thing going with the band. When we was playing at the old Cotton Club, I used to pay off then. The salary was sixty-six dollars and sixty-six cents. I used to have to go the bank every day...I used to go to the cashier and draw the amount of money I needed to get change. Because the first couple of times I paid them, I was owing this guy six cents, another guy sixty-six cents,

the other guy sixty cents, and I don't know... So I got the idea, my mathematics told me to take out how many pennies I needed, how much change I needed. So I used to go by the bank that morning and get my change, and then I'd pay the guys off.

And I had the idea, I brought it with the guys... Because you know, in the beginning, it was a corporate band. So I told them, I said, "Let's get together and start a savings account." I wanted to start it out with five dollars a week. And that's all that was put... Because you know, if ten guys put in five dollars a week, that's fifty-five dollars. [SIC: $50] So I said, "Let's put in five dollars a week and start a bank account of our own." I said, "Then we can keep from having to go to Cab and borrow money. We can borrow money from ourselves." I did it for about two weeks, and then the guys started to squawkin' about it.
